name: clove-hitch
draw: Rope wrapped twice around a horizontal pole with the two turns crossing in an X over the front and both ends leaving below.

name: round-turn-hitch
draw: Rope taking a full round turn around a ring or rail, then tied off on its own standing part with two stacked half hitches.

name: sheet-bend
draw: Two ropes of different thickness joined: a thick rope folded into a U bight with a thinner rope looping around it and tucked under itself.

name: timber-hitch
draw: Rope looped around a log with its tail twisted back around itself several times along the log's top.

name: trucker-hitch
draw: Rope running from a small loop down around a hook below and back up through the loop, pulled tight like a pulley, on a load edge.

name: taut-line-hitch
draw: Rope looped around a tent stake, its tail wrapped twice inside the loop and once more outside, forming an adjustable loop.

name: sheepshank
draw: Rope with a slack section folded into an S of three parallel strands, each end bight held by a half hitch.

name: overhand-knot
draw: Single rope with one simple overhand loop tied in the middle, the two ends leaving in opposite directions.

name: monkey-fist-knot
draw: Round ball of woven rope turns in a three way basket pattern with a single rope tail coming out.

name: fishermans-knot
draw: Two parallel rope ends each tied in an overhand knot around the other, the two knots sliding together in the middle.

name: carrick-bend
draw: Two ropes interwoven in a flat symmetrical diamond pattern of over and under crossings, ends leaving on opposite sides.

name: prusik-knot
draw: Small closed loop of cord wrapped three times around a thicker vertical rope, the loop hanging down.

name: alpine-butterfly-knot
draw: Rope running horizontally with a fixed teardrop loop standing up from a twisted knot in its middle.

name: turks-head-knot
draw: Braided rope band woven around a cylinder in a repeating over and under wave pattern, like a ring.

name: cow-hitch
draw: Rope bight passed through a ring with both ends pulled back through the loop, forming a lark's head on the ring.

name: clinch-knot
draw: Fishing line threaded through a hook eye and twisted around itself five times, the tag end tucked back through the first loop.

name: slip-knot
draw: Rope tied with an overhand knot around a bight, leaving an adjustable loop that pulls closed from the long end.

name: constrictor-knot
draw: Rope wrapped tightly around a round post with a crossing turn and a tucked end trapped under a diagonal riding turn.

name: zeppelin-bend
draw: Two ropes each curled into a loop, the loops overlapping and locked together with the ends passing through the center in opposite directions.

name: blood-knot
draw: Two fishing lines joined by tight barrel shaped twists on each side of a central gap where the ends poke out.

name: eye-splice
draw: Rope end bent back into a fixed eye loop, the strands woven into the standing part with a tapered braided section.

name: rope-whipping
draw: Rope end with a band of tight thin twine wraps near the tip to stop the strands fraying.

name: flemish-coil
draw: Rope laid flat on a deck in a tight flat spiral like a coiled snail shell, seen from above.

name: chain-sinnet
draw: Rope crocheted into a chain of linked loops running in a straight line, like a daisy chain.

name: ocean-plait-mat
draw: Oval flat mat woven from one rope in a tight over and under lattice pattern.

name: square-lashing
draw: Two poles crossed at right angles and bound together with rope turns wrapped around the joint.

name: marlinspike
draw: Long tapered steel spike with a rounded head end, used for opening rope strands.

name: splicing-fid
draw: Smooth tapered wooden cone with a pointed tip and a rounded base, used for opening rope strands.

name: sailmaker-palm
draw: Leather hand strap worn across the palm with a round metal thimble plate at the base of the thumb.

name: knot-board
draw: Rectangular framed board displaying a grid of different small rope knots mounted on it.

name: rope-fender
draw: Pear shaped fender made of densely braided rope, hanging from a short rope loop.

name: rat-guard
draw: Round metal disc clamped around a diagonal mooring line running from a ship to the quay.

name: cargo-net
draw: Square net of thick rope mesh gathered at the four corners onto a single lifting hook, holding boxes.

name: can-buoy
draw: Flat topped cylindrical buoy floating upright on wavy water, a lateral channel marker.

name: nun-buoy
draw: Cone topped buoy floating upright on wavy water, pointed at the top, a lateral channel marker.

name: spar-buoy
draw: Long thin pole shaped buoy floating upright, most of it below a wavy waterline.

name: bell-buoy

name: whistle-buoy

name: mooring-buoy
draw: Round ball buoy on the water with a metal ring on top and a chain running down to the seabed.

name: isolated-danger-mark

name: safe-water-mark
draw: Round buoy with vertical stripes and a single sphere topmark on a short pole.

name: cardinal-mark
draw: Pillar buoy with two stacked cone topmarks, one pointing up and one pointing down, and a wide band across the body.

name: special-mark-buoy
draw: Pillar buoy topped with a single X shaped cross topmark.

name: lobster-buoy
draw: Small bullet shaped foam float with a spindle stick through it and a rope trailing down.

name: buoy-tender
draw: Work ship with a large deck crane on its foredeck lifting a navigation buoy out of the water.

name: daybeacon
draw: Single post standing in water carrying a flat triangular sign board on top.

name: surface-marker-buoy
draw: Tall narrow inflatable sausage tube floating upright on the water with a thin line going down.

name: racing-mark-buoy
draw: Inflatable pyramid shaped racing mark floating on the water with a small anchor line below.

name: boat-navigation-lights

name: ship-lantern

name: range-lights
draw: Two lights on posts on the shore, one short in front and one tall behind, aligned with a dashed sight line to a boat.

name: sector-light

name: screw-pile-lighthouse

name: skeleton-tower-lighthouse

name: caisson-lighthouse

name: pierhead-light
draw: Short round light tower at the end of a harbor pier with a lamp on top and waves beside it.

name: fresnel-lens
draw: Beehive shaped lighthouse lens made of stacked glass rings around a central lamp, on a base.

name: mooring-bitts
draw: Pair of short thick iron posts on a shared base plate with a rope wound around them in a figure eight.

name: fairlead-chock

name: hawsepipe
draw: Ship bow seen from the side with an anchor pulled up snug into a round opening in the hull, chain going inside.

name: concrete-tetrapod
draw: Chunky concrete block with four stubby legs pointing out in different directions, a breakwater unit.

name: groyne
draw: Row of wooden posts and planks running from the beach out into the waves, sand piled on one side.

name: sea-wall

name: floating-dry-dock

name: marine-fuel-dock

name: shore-power-pedestal
draw: Short post on a marina dock with a power socket, a light on top and a cable running to a boat.

name: mooring-dolphin

name: boat-hook

name: mooring-ring

name: mooring-reel

name: ship-cargo-derrick

name: container-twistlock
